haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 and the gateway never touches Redis, so no counter is read or changed.
haiku-low.q2: 100 per minute in total for Standard, because all of a customer's keys share one counter. Enterprise is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q3: 429 with Retry-After in whole seconds and no X-RateLimit headers. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. A request rejected by the check never uses budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The count is taken before forwarding and stays even if the backend returns 500.
haiku-low.q6: It fails open: forwarded with no check, no X-RateLimit headers, ratelimit_store_unavailable emitted, no retry. One extra count is possible.
haiku-low.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise is NOT STATED because its limit is not set yet.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis, under key rl:{customer ID}:{window}. A 60-second TTL set on creation removes old counts.
haiku-low.q9: It resets at each whole-minute boundary, using Redis server time. The window is fixed, not rolling, so there is no gradual recovery.
haiku-low.q10: The check and increment run as one atomic Lua script inside Redis, so no other command can run between them.
haiku-low.q11: It is whole seconds until the next window starts, at least 1, computed by the script from Redis server time. Sent only with 429.
haiku-low.q12: No retry happens. The request is forwarded with no X-RateLimit headers, and ratelimit_store_unavailable is emitted.

sonnet.q1: The gateway returns 401. Redis is not touched, so no counter is read or changed.
sonnet.q2: All of a customer's keys share one counter and one budget, so the total is the plan's limit per minute (100 per minute for Standard). Enterprise is not set.
sonnet.q3: The client gets 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header in whole seconds and no X-RateLimit headers. The request is never forwarded, so the backend does not see it.
sonnet.q4: No. A rejected request leaves the counter alone and never uses budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The count was taken before the forward and stays even if the backend returns 500.
sonnet.q6: It fails open. The gateway forwards the request with no check, adds no X-RateLimit headers, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, and does not retry.
sonnet.q7: Standard is 100 requests per minute. The Enterprise limit is not set yet (Product has not decided).
sonnet.q8: In Redis, shared by all six gateway instances, under the key rl:{customer ID}:{window}. Each counter has a 60 second TTL, set when the counter is created, and Redis deletes it when the TTL ends.
sonnet.q9: At the next whole-minute boundary, by Redis server time (fixed window). The new window uses a new counter key, and the old counter expires by TTL.
sonnet.q10: The check_and_incr Lua script runs inside Redis as one atomic step. The check and the increment cannot be split, and all instances use the same counter.
sonnet.q11: It is the whole seconds until the next window starts, at least 1. The Lua script computes it from Redis server time and it is sent only with 429.
sonnet.q12: No retry. Each later request tries Redis again, waiting up to 50 ms. The client gets no X-RateLimit headers, so it gets no rate-limit information.
